business: Online distributor of electronic components for small manufacturers
target: small and mid-size electronics manufacturers and repair shops that buy components in low volumes, today from a big catalogue distributor or a local wholesaler

segments.name: Contract electronics manufacturer (small PCB assembly shop)
segments.how: Buys hundreds of line items a month against customer BOMs; a missing part stops a production line.

segments.name: Product company with its own hardware (IoT, instruments)
segments.how: Engineers pick parts; procurement orders them; quality cares about traceability and counterfeits.

segments.name: Industrial repair and maintenance shop
segments.how: Urgent one-off needs, pays by card, cares about same-day shipping more than price.

segments.name: University lab or R&D team
segments.how: Small orders, slow approval, needs an invoice and a purchase-order process.

roles.name: Procurement manager
roles.cares: unit price, payment terms (net 30 or better), one supplier instead of five, no surprises on duties and freight

roles.name: Design or production engineer
roles.cares: the exact part number in stock, datasheets and alternates, lead time they can trust

roles.name: Quality manager
roles.cares: genuine parts with traceable manufacturer sourcing, certificates of conformance, a return process

roles.name: Owner or finance lead
roles.cares: total cost, credit terms, the risk of a new supplier failing mid-project

situations.name: Loyal to a big catalogue distributor
situations.how: Everything works, prices are high, shipping from abroad takes a week or more.

situations.name: Burned by a counterfeit or a late shipment recently
situations.how: Actively looking, but trust is the whole question.

situations.name: Buys from several local wholesalers
situations.how: Cheap but chaotic: no stock visibility, cash payments, no paperwork.

situations.name: New line starting, no supplier chosen yet
situations.how: Open to anyone who can quote a full BOM quickly.

objections: How do we know the parts are genuine and not re-marked?
Our current distributor gives us net 45; will you?
If it's not in stock today, why would we wait for you instead of ordering from the catalogue giant?
Who are you? We have never heard of you and a wrong part costs us a production day.
Your prices are only a bit lower and switching means new vendor paperwork and QA approval.
Can you quote a 200-line BOM in a day, or is this a webshop for hobbyists?
What happens when a part is end-of-life? Do you suggest alternates?
Do you handle import duties, or do we get a customs bill later?
triggers: a line stop last month because a part arrived late
the finance lead asked procurement to cut component spend by 10%
a new product going into production this quarter
the incumbent distributor raised minimum order values
regions: an industrial town two hours away
